subject: Private endpoint egress delegation & proxy playbook
messages:
From: Paul Evans <paul.evans@netwell.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Netwell Ops <ops@netwell.com>, security@medsys.com
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress — delegation options and requested IPs

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood Private yesterday. As we prepare our firewall and compliance evidence, I need to get firm requirements for outbound connectivity from our VPC to Redwood control plane and model endpoints.

Attached is our initial CSV of candidate egress ranges (netwell-egress-ips.csv). We have two questions:

1) Can Redwood accept connections via our company proxy (Netwell-managed) with a stable egress IP pool (we'd prefer to own/maintain the proxy and advertise fixed IPs to our perimeter)?
2) If we cannot host the proxy, can Redwood provide a dedicated static egress IP or NAT gateway that we can allowlist on our firewall?

Other asks: mTLS requirements, port list, DNS names that need allowlisting, and whether Redwood requires PTR records for IP ownership evidence. We will need a short checklist we can hand to Network Ops and our compliance team.

Can you confirm the options and include a short playbook we can follow? We've attached the CSV and labeled items we think are mandatory.

Thanks,
Paul Evans
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Netwell Health

Attachments: netwell-egress-ips.csv (CSV)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Evans <paul.evans@netwell.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — delegation options and requested IPs

Paul — thanks, this is helpful. Two viable models from Redwood's side:

Option A — Customer-hosted proxy (Netwell-managed) - You host an outbound proxy (reverse proxy/NAT) with stable IPs. Redwood can terminate TLS to our control plane over that proxy. We will validate TLS client certs if you provide a mTLS endpoint. Pros: you keep IP ownership and audit controls. Cons: you must operate HA proxy, rotate certs, and provide logs.

Option B — Redwood-managed egress (dedicated static IPs) - We provision a per-customer egress NAT or proxy with a small fixed pool of static IPs. You allowlist those IPs on your firewall. Pros: minimal operations for Netwell; we take ownership of IP rotation windows and connectivity. Cons: requires a contractual note about IP change windows and maintenance windows.

Minimum technical checklist (draft):
- Protocols/Ports: outbound TLS 443 to control plane + model endpoints; optional outbound 80 for health checks only.
- DNS: control-plane.redwood.ai and model-hosts.*.redwood.ai (we will provide CNAMEs).
- mTLS: supported on customer-hosted proxy (Option A) and on mutually agreed endpoints for Option B.
- PTR: we can provide signed attestations of IP ownership for Option B; for Option A you must provide PTR/ARIN ownership evidence for your IPs.
- Logging: request for request/response-level logging retention policy (we can provide per-route logs on request).

Next steps:
1) Tell us your preferred option (A or B).
2) If A: share the proxy's IP list and certificate CN you'd like to use.
3) If B: we'll provision a draft static IP range and provide a 72h notice before any maintenance change.

I've attached a one-page delegation checklist (delegation-checklist.pdf) and will circulate a proxy template if you prefer Option A.

Would you be available for a 30m call tomorrow to finalize?

—Markus
Markus Klein
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: delegation-checklist.pdf (PDF)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Evans <paul.evans@netwell.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — delegation options and requested IPs

Paul, Markus — adding the security checklist items we've used for other Private customers. This should help your compliance and ops teams map rules quickly.

High-level security requirements (to include in your firewall policy):
- Inbound: none required for private endpoints (connections are outbound from your VPC).
- Outbound allowlist: only the IPs/CNAMEs provided by Redwood for control plane and model endpoints.
- Ports: TLS 443 required. Allow ephemeral high ports if you plan health/monitoring through a sidecar (document if used).
- mTLS: If you run Customer Proxy (Option A) enable mTLS between proxy and Redwood using a mutually trusted CA. Use cert rotation schedule <= 365 days.
- DNS resolution: whitelist control-plane.redwood.ai and the model-hosted CNAMEs; do not hardcode IPs except in firewall rules as needed.
- PTR & IP ownership: For Option B we provide signed attestations + ARIN allocation info upon request. For Option A provide PTR + ownership proof for your egress IPs.
- Logging and audit: require that either Netwell or Redwood provide 90 days of connection-level logs; for higher risk workloads consider 1 year.

Recommended firewall rule examples (minimal):
- Allow TCP 443 -> control-plane.redwood.ai (resolved IPs) from the private-subnet ranges (10.0.0.0/16).
- Allow TCP 443 -> model-hosts.us.redwood.ai range (list provided) from compute subnets.
- Deny all other outbound ports to external IPs excluding approved monitoring endpoints.

Proxy configuration template attached (proxy-config-template.yaml) — this includes header passthrough, client cert validation, and health-check endpoints. If you opt for Option A, we can pre-validate your config in a short runbook.

Thanks — happy to run the call and walk Ops through the template.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proxy-config-template.yaml (YAML)

Laura / Markus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the checklist. After internal review we prefer Option A (Netwell-managed proxy) so we keep egress ownership in-house. A couple of follow-ups:

- We'll prepare the proxy IP list and PTR evidence by EOD Monday and share the CSV.
- We need Redwood to confirm whether you need the proxy to present a client cert (mTLS) or whether a mutual TLS tunnel to a Redwood ingress is sufficient.
- Can Redwood run a short config validation against our proxy template before we go to production?

Next step: schedule a 30-minute handoff call next Wednesday 09/15 at 11:00am PT if that works for you. We'll loop in Netwell Ops (egress-operations@netwell.com).
